    train_cfg = config["training"]

        betas=tuple(train_cfg.get("betas", [0.9, 0.95])),

def make_scheduler(optimizer, config: Dict[str, Any]):
    from torch.optim.lr_scheduler import CosineAnnealingLR, LinearLR, SequentialLR

    train_cfg = config["training"]

    warmup = LinearLR(optimizer, start_factor=1e-8, end_factor=1.0, total_iters=warmup_steps)

    """Pad tensor along dim=1 to max_len."""

    cumsum = torch.cumsum(att_masks, dim=1)
    att_2d = cumsum[:, None, :] <= cumsum[:, :, None]

```python
tokenizer = get_tokenizer_from_policy(model)
```

I can fix this by checking if the model has a `.policy` attribute in evaluate.py and extracting it before passing to `get_tokenizer_from_policy`, or I could modify `get_tokenizer_from_policy` itself to handle this wrapper type. The simplest approach is adding a conditional check at line 382 to unwrap the policy when needed. Applying the fix now...
